evidence_kind: Matching native PE/PDB static instructions and retained REA pseudocode; no original-engine execution.

selector.procedure: PlayerUnitInput.FindUseable RVA0x20fa20, called by Cursor.CheckUseTarget RVA0x191a80
selector.eligibility: Current actual owner and Interact; first actual group visible; Interact.IsUseableBy with the real player. CursorOnly and UseExtents select the supported screen polygon path.
selector.projection: Screen UseExtents uses actual screen cursor XY, owner parallax, source polygon and owner Z projection. Current consumer admits parallax1 and Z0; other branches reject explicitly.
selector.polygon_priority: Higher signed draw-group index wins; for the same group only strictly smaller float squared distance to Interact.GetUseLocation wins. Exact ties depend on native pointer-hash traversal order.
selector.text_order: In the CursorOnly UseExtents branch, the UseTextBoxes component-rectangle checks occur after and outside the polygon priority gate. Any matching text rectangle writes the current owner, distance and group as winner. Treating all text matches as polygon-priority matches changes native behavior.
selector.portable_ambiguity_policy: Reject multiple matching text owners. With one matching text owner, reject another polygon hit with strictly higher group/distance priority because result depends on which candidate native hash traversal visits last. Otherwise that sole text owner wins. With polygon-only hits, reject exact best-priority ties.
selector.location: GetUseLocation RVA0x2c0270 honors Body/primary flip for offsets. Its CursorOnly branch uses actual GetZLocation times float0.8660254 plus OffsetY, not an inferred screen-center Y. The consumer reuses the existing actual InteractionWorld.useLocation.
selector.indexing_limit: The portable selector scans actual registered source records and performs actual geometry predicates. It does not reconstruct the proprietary cursor-grid container/hash layout. Global UseableOffScreen cursor records and nonextent range paths reject.

polygon_point.operation: Initialize previous vertex from the final polygon point; compare each vertexY>=pointY. When previous/current comparisons differ, compare float(previousX-currentX)*(currentY-pointY) >= float(currentX-pointX)*(previousY-currentY). Toggle parity when that comparison equals currentAbove. Separate float products; no contraction.
polygon_point.boundary: Do not replace these >= comparisons with a generic half-open ray or a rectangle predicate: polygon-edge membership is a distinct native policy.

text_rectangle.operation: Integer x+width and y+height are converted to float after addition. Left/top inclusive, right/bottom exclusive. Portable malformed negative/overflowing extents reject.

cursor_state.previous_target: Resolve current public owner ID in actual World lookup; a missing positive cached ID is cleared and forces reevaluation. Portable keys also retain the actual entity lifetime.
cursor_state.repeat: Only RepeatDelay>0 activates this branch. When Select flags bit2 is absent, reset actual Interact repeatTimer to RepeatDelay. Otherwise subtract the input elapsed; strict timer<0 sets repeat and adds RepeatInterval once. Exactly zero is not expiration.
cursor_state.reevaluate: Previous owner missing, Select pressed bit4, repeat expiration, either actual cursor coordinate differs from previous coordinate, or ForceUseCheck. ForceUseCheck is cleared before the GUI-blocker/query branch.
cursor_state.input_clock: InputHandler.HandleInput RVA0x194b49 preserves its second float argument and forwards it unchanged to Cursor.HandleInput at RVA0x194ce1/0x194ce7. Cursor forwards it to CheckUseTarget. No owner/world multiplier is applied inside the cursor repeat branch; the exact top-level native clock producer remains outside this retained evidence.
cursor_state.enabled_candidate: Call HighlightOn first. Then CursorOnly and (Select pressed or repeat or AutoActivate or (!native UseMouse and AutoActivateWithGamepad)) calls actual Interact.Use with null Unit user.
cursor_state.order: New candidate HighlightOn and possible Use occur before processing old-target HighlightOff/OnMouseOff and writing the new cached target. A GUI blocker still routes target change to null and old-target cleanup.
cursor_state.old_highlight_off: On target change, requires actual old Interact, actual old primary, old Interact.enabled, and (old primary name differs from HighlightOnAnimation or FloatHighlightAnimation). Disabled-old-target behavior is not equivalent to unconditional HighlightOff.
cursor_state.callbacks: Old target ScriptManager.OnMouseOff RVA0x28b7d0 is gated by Thing.IsPhysicallyVisible RVA0x2e62d0. New visible target dispatches actual OnMouseOver source matches with fresh CreatedThisFrame=(World.time<=Thing.creationTime), then writes cursor target ID. These are distinct from PlayerUnitInput OnActiveUseTarget callbacks.
cursor_state.reevaluation_scope: FindUseable, enabled-target HighlightOn and possible Use all execute only inside the reevaluation predicate. They still execute when the selected target is the same as the previous target. Old/new callbacks and cached-ID change are separately gated on new!=old.
cursor_state.OnMouseOff_payload: ScriptManager.OnMouseOff RVA0x28b7d0 invokes matching Script.run(owner,emptyString,defaultLuaTable). No UserId, AttachedTable or CreatedThisFrame field is added by this event producer; generic Script.run source fields remain separate.
cursor_state.physical_visibility: Thing.IsPhysicallyVisible RVA0x2e62d0 requires Body base-color alpha byte>0, Body scalar scale at+0x48>0, actual primary, primary.GetScale(true)>0, and primary.GetDrawColor alpha byte>0. It does not itself test group visibility, renderer cull or a guessed viewport.
cursor_state.callback_payload_source_fields: Script.run RVA0x24f610 adds triggeredById/TriggeredByTable for the actual owner. It adds name only for a nonempty string argument (RVA0x24f6dc..0x24f6fa, repeated alternate branch). Cursor OnMouseOver and OnMouseOff both pass the empty string, so neither event should inject name=typeName; source matching remains actual Thing matching.
cursor_state.portable_input_source: Android/host adaptation: a newly pressed logical hardware Select edge changes input mode to non-pointer. An actual setLocalCursor sample changes it to pointer. Repeated held hardware snapshots retain that newer pointer mode; they must not relabel it every simulation tick. The edge uses consumed local-action history, which excludes pointer-injected Select snapshots.

highlight.floating_on: When FloatHighlightAnimation is true and actual retained highlight pointer is null, MANAGERS[0].Create RVA0x29e350 receives HighlightOnAnimation and the actual owner Thing. Retain the returned actual animation. If owner UseScreenLocation is true, call Animation.SetUseScreenLocation RVA0x297830. An existing retained pointer suppresses recreation/restart.
highlight.floating_off: If retained highlight exists, set Animation.mCanceled at+0x63; mark attached Thing dirty when the actual native attachment/animation flag requires it; clear retained Interact highlight pointer. Actual manager completion owns deferred finish/fade; do not replace this with immediate destruction.

limitations: Static evidence does not establish physical touch/controller behavior or native GPU geometry parity.
Candidate hit rectangles depend on the actual retained text-layout provider; its existing documented paragraph-layout approximation remains separate.
Gamepad free-form navigation, native mouse scaling/camera/parallax branches, global cursor useables and exact pointer-hash order remain unsupported.
Exact native arbitration between multiple distinct hardware/pointer events arriving inside one fixed simulation interval is not established by this edge-based input-source adaptation.
